threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Question:
My name is registered in good standing with ICCRC.
My client has two years of Canadian work experience as a Religious Worker (NOC 4217) on an employer-specific work permit. There are employment periods when he did not receive any direct payment from the employer. According to Buddhist precepts, direct payment is not allowed. Instead, the employer had paid all necessary expenses including international and local transportation, meals, accommodation, medical expenses, and any other expenses.
My questions are as follows:
1. Will my client's Canadian work experience be qualified work experience under Express Entry-Canadian Experience Class (CEC), in terms of the fact that he has received no direct payment from the employer?
Answer: No. For the purposes of Skilled Workers under Economic Classes (Division 1 of Part 6 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations), the definition of work which applies is that defined in subsection 73(2) of the Regulations (included below).
Definition of work for the Division 1 Skilled Workers of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations
73(2) For the purposes of this Division, work means an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned.
2. Are there any specific requirements for forms of payment regarding qualifying work experience under CEC? Will indirectly paid work experience be regarded as paid work experience under CEC?
Answer: Applicants applying through the Express Entry application management system must meet the requirements of one of the Federal Economic Classes managed through Express Entry. Work experience in all three classes must meet the definition of subsection 73(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), which states that work means an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned. The deliberate phrasing of 73(2) and the use of "wages or commissions" generally excludes grants, stipends, and in-kind remuneration.
Wages and commissions are commonly understood to be monetary compensation, from an employer to an employee, for performing an activity. The onus is on the applicant to demonstrate that they were paid wages or commissions for that activity.
3. If my client is ineligible under CEC while he still wants to apply to CEC using his current work experience, will he be
eligible to apply for H&C exemption?
Answer: The foreign national cannot request Humanitarian and compassionate considerations to overcome the eligibility requirements for one of the Federal Economic Classes managed through Express Entry as a result of Section 25(1.2)(a.1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act which states the Minister may not examine the request if the request is for an exemption from any of the criteria or obligations of Division 0.1. Experience which does not meet the definition of skilled work, including the requirement that it be paid, should not be included in your client's Express Entry profile. We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Digital Signatures -- REP-2021-0788

Question: Does IRCC accept Digital Signatures for the following applications: spousal files, the essential pathways,
citizenship, PNP approved files uploaded via online portal, temporary residence (visitor, work, study) overseas?
Answer: As is outlined on our website, a physical or scanned signature is not required for online application forms for Immigration to Canada (Express Entry, PNP through Express Entry, Temporary Residence). Clients can simply upload the required documents to their account. After they have uploaded all the necessary forms, a “next" button will appear at the bottom of the page. Once clicked, clients will be prompted to enter their name as it appears on their application form, and answer a security question which, together, will be understood as their electronic signature for the entirety of their application. However, one form that requires a physical signature regardless of whether it is submitted online or on paper is the Use of Representative form (IMM5476). As such, this form would have to be printed, signed, scanned and uploaded.
For Family Class Application forms, IRCC will accept scanned/photocopied versions of the forms and their corresponding handwritten signatures when applicants (the sponsor and their sponsored family members) reside in different countries. For all family class application forms, the signature(s) must still be a physically signed copy (e.g. copy of a handwritten signature) rather than a digital signature. The Department accepts photocopies of the family class application forms,-however sponsors or applicants may be asked to provide the original copy of any of the forms with the original handwritten signatures if an IRCC
officer determines it is necessary.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.question:

Question:
Good afternoon,
Would you please clarify whether a foreign national who is working full time in a NOC A, B or O occupation in Canada while on implied status (between a study permit and a post-graduate work permit) can count that time as qualifying Canadian work experience for the purpose of a PR application under the Canadian Experience Class.
In this particular scenario, during the implied status period the person is authorized to work full time without a work permit while waiting for a decision on the PGWP pursuant to paragraph 186(w) of the Regulations. The PDIs do not contemplate this particular scenario and simply state that applicants must have temporary status during the qualifying period of work experience gained in Canada. The PDIs do state note:
Work experience acquired while under implied status will be considered as eligible work experience under the CEC, provided the applicant continued to work in Canada under the same conditions as their original work permit until a decision
was made on their application for a work permit extension ([https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-)
citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/permanent-residence/economic- classes/experience/qualifying-work-experience.html).
However, in this case, the foreign national is transitioning from a study permit to a work permit, with authorization to work full time without a work permit in the interim. The work experience in question was not gained while they were a full-time student, so in my view, they should be able to count the work experience while on implied status towards qualifying Canadian work experience in a PR application under the CEC. Kindly let me know if my interpretation is correct.
Answer:
They may use the work experience obtained on the PGWP and, if they genuinely had implied status, that work experience could be counted as well provided it meets all other requirements.

threads.subject: Express Entry: CEC Experience -- REP-2021-0815
threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Question:
Dear Sir/Madam,
We have a question regarding a prospective client.
Client has received the invitation under CEC class and want to retain us for PR application. Before we accept client we want make sure client is eligible for express entry and meets all requirements. I was looking but was not able to find exact information.
So I will give brief description about the scenario related to clients experience:
Scenario: Client has been working in Canada in NOC B for more than year and half. Her work hours were disruptive due to COVID. For Example: Client worked fulltime 2 weeks than part time for 1 week than off no work for one week than again fulltime for 1 week and so on. So client experience is all in a similar manner. But overall hours that client has worked are more than 1560 hours.
From (dd-mm-yyyy) To (dd-mm-yyyy)Employment Basis Hours Worked per Week
01-12-2019 25-01-2020 Full time 30 Hours 26-01-2020 26-02-2020 Part Time Average 22 hours 23-02-2020 07-03-2020 Full Time 30 Hours 08-03-2020 22-08-2020 Part TimeAverage 18 hours 23-08-2020 31-10-2020 Full Time 30 Hours 01-11-2020 09-01-2021 Part Time Average 24 hours 10-01-2021 25-05-2021 Full Time 30 Hours Total Hours = More than 1560
Please confirm if she can consider her this experience to be eligible for 1 Year CEC experience. If yes, what documents should we provide to prove her experience. Further, we have attached a template employment letter, please review if this would good enough to explain the hours details or should we provide additional details.
Answer:
It would be up to the applicant to calculate their working hours to ensure they meet the minimum work experience requirements before applying. There are a few ways to meet the 1 year of skilled work experience in Canada in the last 2
years before applying, including:
Full-time at 1 job: 30 hours a week for 12 months (1 year full time, or 1,560 hours)
Equal amounts in part-time work: for example 15 hours/week for 24 months (1 year full time, or 1,560 hours). Applicants can work as many part-time jobs as needed to meet this requirement. Fulil-time work at more than 1 job: 30 hours a week for 12 months at more than 1 job (1 year full time, or 1,560 hours).
For all work experience declared, applicants must provide a reference or experience letter from the employer which indicates the number of work hours per week.
Also, please note that an allowance for a reasonable period of vacation time will generally be made in calculating the period of qualifying work experience (e.g., a two-week period of paid vacation leave within a given 52-week period in which the applicant was engaged in qualifying work experience). An allowance for normal vacation time during a period of qualifying work experience cannot be used as a substitute or proxy for meeting the in-Canada element of the work experience requirement (i.e., work experience obtained outside Canada will not be considered as though the applicant had been on a period of vacation in order to be counted as part of the period of in-Canada work experience). While officers will account for a reasonable period of vacation time in calculating the period of qualifying work experience in Canada, each application is considered on its own merits with a final decision based on a review of all the information available to the officer at the time of decision.
The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements. The assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the IRCC examining officer.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.answer:

For example if a paper PNP or AIPP application is submitted but then an Express Entry Canadian Experience Class application is submitted shortly thereafter how are these processed. Would the AIP be processed first with the EE second in the running if the AlP should be unsuccessful OR may the EE application process possibly precede the processing of the AIP.

Answer:
Foreign nationals may apply for multiple immigration programs at once, as long as they have paid the required cost recovery fees for each program to which they have applied. For example, a foreign national could apply under the CEC if invited to do so through Express Entry, and could also apply under the AIP or PNP outside of the Express Entry system.

## Immigration Representatives / Représentants inmigration (IRCC)
Good day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration
Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: CRS points awarded for credentials completed 100% abroad due to Covid-19.
The applicant completed 100% ofher/his study program which started during covid from abroad. I am looking into clarifying if under EE, this applicant will still be awarded the 15-30 points on the CRS points where it refers to Canadian Credentials.
I have received different answers from the call centre which indicated that internal guide has been updated that student would be awarded regardless if they were physically in Canada or not, as long as they have been issued a Letter of Introduction
while on twitter, it has been indicated that only the ones physically in Canada would be awarded.
Answer:
For Express Entry, there have been no changes to how CRS points are awarded for education. A Canadian educational credential cannot be awarded if the credentials were obtained in a study or training program in which distance learning amounted to more than half of the program length. To get points the credential must be a “Canadian educational credential," as per R73 and meet one of the definitions of an, “Eligible credential”.
Pursuant to R73.1, a Canadian educational credential means any diploma, certificate or credential, issued on
the completion of a Canadian program of study or training at an educational or training institution that is
recognized by the provincial authorities responsible for registering, accrediting, supervising and regulating such
institutions.
In addition, the credential must meet the requirements stated in the Express Entry Ministerial Instructions — MI
11(3) and MI 30 (1)-(5).

threads.subject: Clarification re Hong Kong PR Program-Distance Learning -- REP-2021-1045
threads.question:
Dear Sir/Madam,
I am writing to seek clarification to the new temporary public policy for PR for Hong Kong residents with regards to Education Requirements when it relates to distance learning inside Canada at a post-secondary designated learning institution (DLI) in Canada.
The Education Requirements state that: Applicants must have graduated from a DLI in the 3 years before they apply (for Stream A) OR from a DLI or with equivalent ECA in the 5 years before they apply (for Stream B) with one of the following:
a post-secondary degree (for example, bachelor's, master's, doctorate)
- a post-secondary diploma for a program of study that is at least 2 years in length a graduate or post-graduate credential for a program that is at least 1 year in length and
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
the program required them to have a post-secondary degree or diploma as a prerequisite and they graduated from their post-secondary degree or diploma no more than 5 years before the start of the graduate or post-graduate program
Furthermore for Stream A: The program of study can be completed in any field of study, with at least 50% of the program of study completed while physically present in Canada, either in class or online.
My question is, if a Hong Kong foreign national holding a valid work permit inside Canada completes a distance learning (study permit should not be required) eligible credential from a DLi while being physically present in Canada for more than 50% of the program duration within the prescribed period, would this applicant meet the Education Requirements to apply under the program?
Any guidance of the above would be greatly appreciated.
Thank you very much for your time and attention.
Respectfully,
threads.answer:
Hello,
Note that the information provided below may be of assistance but please note that we do not respond to case-specific enquiries.
To be eligible for permanent residence under stream A of the temporary public policy for Hong Kong residents, applicants must have graduated from a post-secondary designated learning institution in Canada, obtained eligible credentials as indicated on our website, and must have completed at least 50% of the program while physically present in Canada, either in person (in class) or online. Applicants may be eligible if the program of study was completed through distance learning while being physically present in Canada for at least 50% of the program of study and while being legally authorized to study in Canada.
Since by definition distance learning does not require one to be in Canada, a study permit cannot be issued for this type of course. For example, if a foreign national authorized to work in Canada is prohibited from engaging in studies as per a condition of their work permit, they are allowed to engage in distance learning courses. However, some distance learning courses include an in-Canada portion to the program (e.g., special tutorials or the writing of final exams). If the overall course of study is greater than six months, then the student requires a study permit for the in-Canada portion of the program, even if the in-Canada portion is less than six months.
We trust this information will assist you.
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Dear
Thank you for your enquiry.
In fact, the IMM 5476 was not modified in April 2021. It was modified in July 2021 and the April date was an error when the change was made in July. The last previous change to the IMM 5476 was in February 2021.
There is currently no single, IRCC-wide policy for the grace period for previous versions when forms are modified, though IRCC has been studying this issue. Currently, as regards the IMM 5476, IRCC advises immigration professionals of changes, as well as of the grace period for previous versions, via their professional bodies.
There is no exception to the grace period date for the IMM 5476. Even if a modification appears only “cosmetic", there would be greater confusion for users of the form, both compensated and uncompensated, and for IRCC’s various processing offices and the Client Service Centre, if an exception was made in the case of one change, but not for the other.
We trust that this responds to your query.
Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Clients have been entering Canada after having changed DLIs and without applying for a new study permit (often because they don't have time to reapply) and have been issued their permits without any problems.

threads.answer:
Hello,
Thank you for your inquiry.
Requests to change DLls after applying for a study permit
Outside Canada Students may request to change their DLl prior to entering Canada if their visa or electronic travel authorization (eTA) has not yet been
approved by IRCC.
If the student changed their DLl after submitting their study permit application and the application is still in progress, the student may submit their new letter of acceptance via the IRCC Web form. If their isa or eTA has already been approved, the student should submit a new application and pay the appropriate fees online or at the visa application centre.
Inside Canada
Students engaging in post-secondary studies in Canada may transfer between institutions (both public and private) or change their course or program of study without applying for a change to the condition of their study permit, as long as the receiving institution is a DLI. Students should notify IRCC through their MyAccount when they transfer to another DLI
Students who transfer to a DLI that doesn't have an approved COVID-19 readiness plan and decide to leave Canada may not be able to return because their DLl is not on the approved list.

threads.subject: Change of passport and FRL -- REP-2021-1177
threads.question:
Dear Officer,
Where a foreign national who requires a Family Reunification Letter (FRL) to come to Canada and travelling with the passport of a country which is visa-exempt changes passport (e.g. because their passport is lost and must be replaced or has been replaced as it was soon to expire) what is the status of the FRL which was applied for with the previous passport?
I understand that the passport is intimately tied to an eTA (and that a new eTA would be required where the passport was replaced) but it is not clear to what extent the eTA and the FRL are tied to one another.
Would it make a difference if the foreign national retained the passport which had been updated (and had been cancelled), for example?
Thank you in advance for your clarification of this matter.
Sincerely,
threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Answer:
To avoid any difficulties along the travel continuum given that the family reunification letter references the foreign national's passport number, we recommend they request a new family reunification letter if their passport number changes.
Also, please note that if a client were to re-apply for an eTA and should their application require further review by an officer, the client would need to self-identify to IRCC as meeting a travel restriction exemption to request priority processing of their application. We trust that this information will assist you
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.question:
Good day
Thank you for contacting us and for your patience with this request.
Question Is there any restriction on (1) a Canadian employer listing a refugee claimant on a low-wage LMiA application and, in turn, (2) on a refugee claimant applying for an LMIA-based employer-specific work permit?
Answer Refugee claimants are eligible for an open work permit under R206 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations
(IRPR).
f they wish to apply for an extension of their work permit under a Labour Market Impact Assessment (e.g., at the request of an employer), they may apply for a work permit extension; however, such an application would remain under R206 of the Regulations and would not confer or extend status under R183(5), as they do not have status.
In other words, a refugee claimant cannot move from a work permit that does not confer temporary resident status to a work permit that does confer status.
We trust you will find this information useful.
Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox
